newsitem.title: CHINA: China to adjust steel product output.
newsitem.headline: China to adjust steel product output.

text.p: China is to adjust its steel production mix to reduce imports and meet growing domestic demand for other varieties, especially value-added products, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
China aims to produce 2.0 million tonnes of high value-added steel products to replace costly imports, it quoted an official of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry as saying.
China is expected to produce 88 million tonnes of rolled steel this year, up by 2.5 million tonnes from 1996 but still not enough to satisfy demand, estimated at 98 million tonnes last year, he said.
China imported more than 15 million tonnes of rolled steel last year and imports this year were expected to remain at similar levels, he said.

"We need to develop cold rolling plates used for automobiles, refrigerators, washing machines and microwave ovens, which use a lot of imported material," the newspaper quoted the unidentified official as saying.
Production of steel bars used for heavy-duty and light rail tracks and for building materials was no longer a problem, but China had low output of steel plates and tubes, he said.
China produced 100 million tonnes of steel last year, making it the world's biggest manufacturer.
